title: Signal-driven Optimization Triage and Response SLAs for Enterprise Requests
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Establish a signal-driven intake and SLA-based routing system for optimization/advisory requests (batching, caching, quant profiles, routing policies). Objective: reduce time-to-first-response for enterprise customers, prioritize high-cost/regression-risk workloads, and automate routing to self-serve guidance, concierge advisory, or engineering engagements.
background: We receive frequent enterprise requests to tune inference economics: batching/caching knobs, quantization requests, and routing policy changes. Current intake is inconsistent: some tickets land with minimal signals (stack traces, payload samples) and sit in Backlog; high-impact requests can be missed or delayed. We need a repeatable funnel that uses signals (token rate, cost delta, latency regression, security constraints) to classify and route requests with defined SLAs.
goals: Define an intake taxonomy with 4 lanes: Self-serve, Concierge (PM/DevRel-assisted), Engineering Triage, Eng Deep Dive
Create an automated scorer for incoming requests using observable signals and customer-provided metadata
Set measurable SLAs for first response and resolution per lane
Integrate routing with Redwood Console (link to route), Support, and Dedicated onboarding
Produce playbooks for common knob changes with recommended guardrails and rollback steps
proposed_solution: 1) Build a lightweight intake form (ticket template) that captures required signals: model, deployment type (hosted/dedicated/private), avg tokens/day, p50/p95 latency, recent cost per 1k tokens, target latency/cost goals, and a minimal sample prompt. 2) Implement a scoring function (rule-based initially) that weights: cost impact (40%), latency regression risk (30%), regulatory/data-sensitivity (15%), repeat occurrence (15%). 3) Map score thresholds to lanes and associated SLAs: Critical (>80) => Eng Deep Dive (first response 24h), High (60-80) => Engineering Triage (48h), Medium (30-60) => Concierge (72h), Low (<30) => Self-serve (10 business days). 4) Attach prescriptive runbooks for common fixes (batch size heuristics, prefix caching template, quant profile recommendation matrix, routing fallback config). 5) Provide an automated triage notification to customer with expected SLA and next steps; surface key metrics in the Console ticket window and create links to the customer's cost/latency dashboard.
decision_notes: Rule-based scorer chosen for MVP to keep implementation fast and auditable; ML-based prioritizer deferred to Q2 after we collect labeled data.
Use existing Support email + Console webhook for intake rather than building a new portal in MVP.
SLA windows chosen to balance engineering capacity and customer expectations; thresholds adjustable after 6 weeks of telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: Intake template deployed and linked from Console and Support page
Automatic scoring and lane assignment executed for 100% of incoming optimization requests
Dashboard shows distribution of requests by lane and SLA compliance metrics
First response SLA achieved >= 90% for Concierge and Engineering Triage lanes during the 30-day pilot
Prescriptive runbook pages for top-4 knob classes published and referenced by >= 30% of Self-serve routed tickets
tasks: PM: finalize intake fields and scoring weights
Design: create intake UI and customer-facing SLA copy
Eng: implement scoring lambda + Console webhook integration
Docs: author runbooks for batching, caching, quantization, and routing
Support: update triage playbook and training for concierge ops
Analytics: build SLA compliance dashboard and request telemetry feeds
risks: False positives: highly scored requests that do not need engineering time could overload Eng capacity
Incomplete signals from customers leading to wrong lane mapping
SLA overcommit if request volume spikes during Dedicated onboarding windows
mitigations: Add mandatory minimal signal fields to intake form and block submission if missing
Introduce a short human-in-the-loop audit step for top-10% scored requests during first 6 weeks
Reserve an emergency eng buffer for Dedicated region launches and autoscale it into the SLA calculations
metrics: Mean time to first response by lane
Avg engineering hours per routed High/Critical ticket
% reduction in repeated follow-ups for the same customer optimization signal
Conversion rate from Self-serve to Concierge (indicates runbook gaps)
